methodological_rigor.justification: The CAPTAIN-1st 5-year analysis is a pre-specified secondary analysis of a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial with stratified randomization and ITT analysis. Proportional hazards assumption was tested (Grambsch-Therneau test) and not violated. Age imbalance between groups is transparently acknowledged and an adjusted HR (0.65) is reported alongside the primary HR (0.74). The EBV DNA clearance analysis is post-hoc and exploratory. The OS analysis lacks multiplicity adjustment (pre-specified secondary endpoint), but the authors appropriately note this. The open-label nature of the OS follow-up (post-unblinding) is a minor limitation. Follow-up exceeds 63 months with 68% OS maturity (180 deaths of 263 enrolled).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This secondary analysis of a phase III RCT (LoE 1b) provides the first 5-year OS evidence for PD-1 inhibitor-based chemoimmunotherapy in RM-NPC, a disease entity with limited long-term data. The absolute 5-year OS benefit of 13.6% (37.8% vs 24.2%) and median OS improvement of 7.9 months are clinically meaningful in a disease with historically poor prognosis. The identification of rapid EBV DNA clearance as a predictive/prognostic biomarker offers actionable guidance for individualized treatment intensification. The findings directly reinforce established guidelines (NCCN, ESMO, CSCO) recommending PD-1 plus chemotherapy as standard first-line treatment.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript adheres to CONSORT guidelines with a trial profile figure, ITT analysis, stratified statistical tests, and comprehensive limitations section. Subgroup analyses are presented with HRs and CIs. The proportional hazards assumption test is explicitly reported. The trial is registered (NCT03707509). The age imbalance is transparently addressed. Survivorship bias in the 2-year completers analysis is appropriately flagged. Primary data are not publicly deposited, consistent with China-based clinical trial norms.

novelty_literature.justification: This is the first 5-year OS data from a phase III trial of PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy in RM-NPC, extending existing 3-year evidence from JUPITER-02 and RATIONALE-309. The EBV DNA clearance as a predictor of 5-year survival is a meaningful extension of prior biomarker work. However, the overall finding—that PD-1 inhibitors improve OS in RM-NPC—is not novel; this study primarily extends the evidence temporally. The establishment of the 37.8% 5-year OS rate as a new benchmark is contextually important for the field.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized with logical progression from background through survival analyses to biomarker findings. Results are reported with appropriate statistical metrics. The EBV DNA clearance findings are well-presented with Kaplan-Meier curves. The limitations section directly addresses age imbalance, survivorship bias in 2-year completers, and lack of multiplicity adjustment. The discussion contextualizes findings within prior NPC immunotherapy trials and is appropriately restrained about the EBV DNA post-hoc analysis.

key_strengths: First 5-year OS evidence from a phase III RCT of PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy in RM-NPC, providing the longest follow-up benchmark in this setting
Pre-specified secondary analysis with mature OS data (68% events), age-adjusted HR analysis, and proportional hazards assumption testing
Clinically meaningful absolute 5-year OS benefit of 13.6% supporting long-term durable benefit in approximately one-third of patients
EBV DNA rapid clearance as a robust biomarker (5-year OS 46.8% vs 7.5%) offering actionable guidance for treatment individualization
key_concerns: Age imbalance between treatment arms (56% vs 43% ≥50 years) suggests potential randomization failure, and adjusted HR (0.65) substantially differs from unadjusted HR (0.74), raising concerns about residual confounding
OS analysis lacks pre-specified multiplicity adjustment; p-value of 0.047 is borderline
EBV DNA clearance analysis is post-hoc and exploratory; causality cannot be established
All patients enrolled in China—generalizability to non-endemic NPC populations with different EBV status and histology is uncertain
Survivorship bias in 2-year camrelizumab completers analysis is acknowledged but the 87.1% 5-year OS in this group may mislead if not carefully contextualized
chief_reviewer.rationale: This well-conducted 5-year update of a phase III RM-NPC trial provides the first long-term survival benchmark for PD-1 chemoimmunotherapy and clinically actionable EBV biomarker data; Tier 2 publication is appropriate given the important extension of evidence in this endemic cancer with mature OS data, though the borderline p-value and age imbalance require careful consideration.
